source.title: The Constitution of India (original question writing)

chapter.name: Fundamental Rights: Your Claim Against the State
chapter.blurb: The idea and list of fundamental rights, equality, freedoms, rights against exploitation and of religion, constitutional remedies, and the limits and amendment of rights.

concepts.name: Limits, emergencies and landmark ideas about rights
concepts.description: Reasonable restrictions, armed forces, the effect of an emergency, the amendment power and the basic structure idea.
concepts.idea: Rights can be limited and amended, but the Supreme Court has held that the basic structure cannot be destroyed.
concepts.rule: Rights come with reasonable restrictions. Article 33 lets Parliament modify these rights for members of the armed forces and similar services. During a national emergency the rights under Article 19 are suspended when the emergency is declared on the ground of war or external aggression, and the President can suspend the right to move the courts for the enforcement of other rights under Article 359; after the 44th Amendment the rights under Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended. Article 368 gives Parliament the power to amend the Constitution. In Golaknath (1967) the Supreme Court held that Parliament could not amend fundamental rights, but in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) it held that Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot change its basic structure.
concepts.example: Article 21 remains available even during an emergency.

questions.q: A proclamation of Financial Emergency under Article 360 has been approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months. Thereafter
questions.a: it continues until it is revoked, without repeated parliamentary approval
o: it continues until it is revoked, without repeated parliamentary approval
it lapses after six months unless Parliament approves it again
it lapses after one year unless Parliament extends it by a special majority
it can continue for a maximum of three years and then must end
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions): Once approved, a Financial Emergency continues indefinitely till revoked: there is no maximum period and no repeated approval is required (p.271).
w: Six-monthly approval is the rule for a National Emergency, not a Financial Emergency (p.271).
No yearly extension is needed; there is no maximum period for a Financial Emergency (p.271).
A three-year ceiling applies to President's Rule, not to a Financial Emergency (p.271).

questions.q: While a Financial Emergency is in operation, the President may issue directions for the reduction of the salaries and allowances of
questions.a: persons serving the Union, including the judges of the Supreme Court and the high courts
o: persons serving the Union, including the judges of the Supreme Court and the high courts
persons serving the Union, but not the judges of the Supreme Court and the high courts
persons serving the states alone, because the Union's own finances remain untouched
persons serving the states and the judges of the high courts, but not the Union's own staff
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions): The President may direct reduction of salaries and allowances of persons serving the Union and of the judges of the Supreme Court and the high courts (p.272).
w: The text expressly includes the judges of the Supreme Court and the high courts (p.272).
The Union's finances are not exempt; the President may order reductions for persons serving the Union (p.272).
Salary directions to persons serving the states are a separate power; here the Union's staff and the judges are covered, not the states' staff alone (pp.271-272).

questions.q: In the S.R. Bommai case (1994) the Supreme Court laid down that, when President's Rule is imposed, the state legislative assembly should be dissolved only after
questions.a: Parliament has approved the presidential proclamation; until then it can only be suspended
o: Parliament has approved the presidential proclamation; until then it can only be suspended
the Governor has submitted a second report confirming the failure of the machinery
the Election Commission has certified that general elections to it cannot be held
one year has elapsed from the date of the proclamation
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions): Bommai proposition 6 (p.269): the assembly may be dissolved only after Parliament approves the proclamation; if Parliament fails to approve, the assembly is reactivated.
w: The Court did not require a second report of the Governor; the President may even act without a report (pp.265, 269).
The Election Commission certificate is the 44th Amendment condition for extending President's Rule beyond one year, not for dissolution (p.266).
The Court tied dissolution to Parliament's approval, not to a waiting period (p.269).

questions.q: During a National Emergency, Article 359 differs from Article 358 in that
questions.a: its suspension of enforcement can be confined to a period shorter than that of the Emergency
o: its suspension of enforcement can be confined to a period shorter than that of the Emergency
it automatically suspends the Fundamental Rights themselves the moment the Emergency is proclaimed
it can be applied only when the Emergency is declared on the ground of war or external aggression
it can also be used to suspend the enforcement of the rights guaranteed by Articles 20 and 21 as well
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions): Article 359 suspends enforcement only for the period specified by the President, which may be the whole Emergency or a shorter period; Article 358 runs for the entire duration (p.264).
w: That describes Article 358, which operates automatically; Article 359 needs a Presidential Order and suspends only enforcement (pp.262-264).
Article 359 operates in both external and internal Emergency; it is Article 358 that is limited to the external one (p.264).
Since the 44th Amendment the President cannot suspend enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 (p.263).

questions.q: A fresh proclamation of National Emergency was not needed at the time of the war against Pakistan in 1965, because
questions.a: the proclamation issued in October 1962 on account of Chinese aggression was still in force
o: the proclamation issued in October 1962 on account of Chinese aggression was still in force
the 1962 proclamation was revoked in January 1965 but the President could revive it without Parliament
the 1962 proclamation had been made on armed rebellion and so covered any later war with any country
Article 352 allows only one proclamation in a decade, so the earlier one served for the later war
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions): The first National Emergency (October 1962) remained in force until January 1968, so no fresh proclamation was needed in 1965 (p.264).
w: Wrong: the 1962 proclamation lasted until January 1968, it was not revoked in 1965 (p.264).
Wrong: the 1962 proclamation was on external aggression (Chinese aggression), not armed rebellion (pp.259, 264).
Wrong: the President may issue different proclamations even when one is already in operation (p.260); the reason in 1965 was that the 1962 one was still in force (p.264).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about President's Rule under Article 356:

1. A proclamation imposing it must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months of its issue.
2. A resolution approving it or its continuance must be passed by a special majority of the House.
3. Once approved it continues for six months and can be extended, with approval every six months, up to a maximum of three years.
4. The President can revoke it at any time by a subsequent proclamation, which needs no parliamentary approval.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions). Statement 1 is correct: p.265. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.265: a simple majority suffices, unlike for a National Emergency. Statement 3 is correct: p.265. Statement 4 is correct: p.266.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.265
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.265
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.265

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Financial Emergency under Article 360:

1. A resolution approving its proclamation, which both Houses must pass, needs only a simple majority of the members present and voting.
2. The proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within one month of its issue.
3. A Financial Emergency was declared during the financial crisis of 1991.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions). Statement 1 is correct: p.271. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.271: the period is two months. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.272: no Financial Emergency has been declared so far, though there was a financial crisis in 1991.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.271
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.271
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.271

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about judicial review of the emergency provisions:

1. The 38th Amendment Act (1975) made the declaration of a National Emergency immune from judicial review, a provision later deleted by the 44th Amendment Act (1978).
2. In Minerva Mills (1980) the Supreme Court held that the proclamation of a National Emergency can be challenged in court on the ground of malafide or reliance on wholly extraneous or irrelevant facts.
3. The 44th Amendment Act retained the 38th Amendment's rule that the President's satisfaction under Article 356 is final and conclusive.
4. In Bommai (1994) the Court held that the burden lies on the Centre to prove that relevant material exists to justify the imposition of President's Rule.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions). Statement 1 is correct: p.260. Statement 2 is correct: p.260. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.269: the 44th Amendment deleted it, so the satisfaction is open to judicial review. Statement 4 is correct: p.269.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.260
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.260
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.260

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the effect of a National Emergency on Centre-state relations:

1. The Centre can give executive directions to a state on any matter.
2. Laws made by Parliament on State List subjects become inoperative six months after the Emergency ceases to operate.
3. The state legislatures stand suspended for the duration of the Emergency.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions). Statement 1 is correct: p.262. Statement 2 is correct: p.262. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.262: their legislative power is not suspended, but is subject to the overriding power of Parliament.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.262
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.262
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.262

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Emergency:

1. The 42nd Amendment Act confined the executive and legislative consequences to the state in which the Emergency is in operation.
2. The life of the Lok Sabha may be extended by a law of Parliament one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases to operate.
3. The President can modify the distribution of revenues between the Centre and the states, the modification lasting till the end of the financial year in which the Emergency ceases to operate.
4. The President can issue ordinances on State List subjects if Parliament is not in session.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions). Statement 1 is incorrect: p.262: it extended them to any other state also. Statement 2 is correct: p.262. Statement 3 is correct: p.262. Statement 4 is correct: p.262.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.262
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.262
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.262

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly's views on the Emergency provisions:

1. Ambedkar observed that the Indian Constitution can be both unitary and federal, according to the requirements of time and circumstances.
2. Mahabir Tyagi opined that the emergency provisions would work as a safety-valve and help in the maintenance of the Constitution.
3. Sir Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar labelled the emergency provisions 'the very life-breath of the Constitution'.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions). Statement 1 is correct: p.259. Statement 2 is correct: p.273. Statement 3 is correct: p.273.
w: '1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.259
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.259
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.259

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the proper and improper use of Article 356, as enlisted in Bommai (1994):

1. Imposition of President's Rule is proper where the ministry is alleged to be maladministering the state or corrupt.
2. It is proper where, after general elections, no party secures a majority in the assembly.
3. It is improper where the governor recommends it without allowing the ministry to prove its majority on the floor of the Assembly.
4. It is proper where the ruling party in the state has suffered a massive defeat in the general elections to the Lok Sabha, as in 1977 and 1980.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions). Statement 1 is incorrect: p.270: maladministration or corruption allegations are listed as improper grounds. Statement 2 is correct: p.270. Statement 3 is correct: p.270. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.270: it is listed among the improper situations.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.270
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.270
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.270

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the effect of a National Emergency on the Fundamental Rights:

1. When an Emergency declared on the ground of war or external aggression ceases to operate, Article 19 revives automatically and a law made during it ceases to have effect to the extent of its inconsistency with Article 19; according to the chapter, no remedy lies for anything done during that Emergency.
2. Since the 44th Amendment, protection from challenge under an Article 359 order extends to all laws made while the order is in force, whether or not they relate to the Emergency.
3. A Presidential Order under Article 359 may extend to the whole country or to only a part of it.
4. A Presidential Order under Article 359 need not be placed before Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions). Statement 1 is correct: p.263. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.263: only laws related to the Emergency are protected. Statement 3 is correct: p.263. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.263: it should be laid before each House of Parliament.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.263
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.263
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.263

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the proclamation of a National Emergency and its approval:

1. The President can proclaim it only on a written recommendation of the cabinet.
2. A resolution approving the proclamation or its continuance can be passed by either House by a simple majority.
3. A resolution disapproving its continuation is required to be passed by the Lok Sabha only, by a simple majority.
4. If one-tenth of the Lok Sabha members give written notice, a special sitting must be held within 14 days to consider a resolution of disapproval.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions). Statement 1 is correct: p.260: 44th Amendment safeguard. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.261: a special majority is needed. Statement 3 is correct: p.261. Statement 4 is correct: p.261.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.260
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.260
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.260

questions.q:
According to Table 12.1 of Laxmikanth, consider the following statements about cases and the elements of the basic structure declared in them:

1. In Kumar Padma Prasad (1992) independence of the judiciary was declared.
2. In Delhi Judicial Service Association (1991) the powers of the Supreme Court under Articles 32, 136, 141 and 142 were declared.
3. In P. Sambamurthy (1986) the rule of law and judicial review were declared.
4. In All India Judge's Association (2001) the unity and integrity of India was declared.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 12 (Basic Structure of the Constitution). Statement 1 is correct: p.202. Statement 2 is correct: p.201. Statement 3 is correct: p.201. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.202: the element was an independent judicial system; unity and integrity is from Raghunath Rao. So exactly 3 are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (2, 3, 4).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (2, 3, 4).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (2, 3, 4).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing National Emergency and President's Rule (Table 17.1):

1. During a National Emergency the state executive and legislature continue to function.
2. Under President's Rule Parliament can delegate the power to make laws for the state to the President.
3. A National Emergency has a maximum prescribed period of three years.
4. President's Rule affects the Fundamental Rights of the citizens.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions). Statement 1 is correct: p.267. Statement 2 is correct: p.267. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.267: it is President's Rule that has a three-year maximum; a National Emergency has none. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.268: it has no effect on Fundamental Rights; it is the National Emergency that affects them. So exactly 2 are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (2, 3).
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (2, 3).
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (2, 3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Emergencies declared so far:

1. The proclamation of June 1975 was made on the ground of armed rebellion.
2. The proclamation of December 1971 was made on the ground of internal disturbance.
3. The second and the third proclamations were both revoked in March 1977.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions). Statement 1 is incorrect: p.264: it was made on the ground of internal disturbance; 'armed rebellion' replaced that phrase only in 1978 (p.260). Statement 2 is incorrect: p.264: it was made in the wake of an attack by Pakistan, on external aggression. Statement 3 is correct: p.264. So exactly 1 is correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 is correct (3).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 is correct (3).
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 is correct (3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Article 356 has become one of the most controversial and most criticised provisions of the Constitution.
Statement-II: Since 1950 President's Rule has been imposed on more than 125 occasions, often in an arbitrary manner for political or personal reasons.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions), p.268: because President's Rule was often imposed arbitrarily for political or personal reasons, Article 356 became one of the most criticised provisions. Statement-II gives the reason for Statement-I.
w: Rejected: Statement-II does explain Statement-I; the book links the arbitrary use to the criticism (p.268).
Rejected: Statement-II is correct (p.268).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct (p.268).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Article 359 does not by itself suspend any Fundamental Right; it only empowers the President to suspend their enforcement.
Statement-II: A Presidential Order under Article 359 can operate both in an Emergency declared on the ground of war or external aggression and in one declared on armed rebellion.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions): Both are correct (p.263 and p.264). The ground of the Emergency does not explain why Article 359 only suspends enforcement; that follows from the way the Article is framed.
w: Rejected: the ground of the Emergency does not explain why Article 359 suspends only enforcement; II does not explain I (pp.263-264).
Rejected: Statement-II is correct (p.264).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct (p.263).

questions.q:
Match the Article in List-I with its subject-matter in Table 17.2 of Laxmikanth, in List-II.

List-I (Article)
A. Article 354
B. Article 355
C. Article 357
D. Article 359A

List-II (Subject)
1. Exercise of legislative powers under a proclamation issued under Article 356
2. Application of the provisions on distribution of revenues while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation
3. Duty of the Union to protect states against external aggression and internal disturbance
4. Application of 'this part' to the state of Punjab (since repealed)
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch. 17 (Emergency Provisions), Table 17.2 (p.273): 354 - revenue distribution during Emergency; 355 - duty of the Union to protect states; 357 - legislative powers under an Article 356 proclamation; 359A - application to Punjab (repealed).
w: A and B are interchanged: 354 concerns revenue distribution and 355 the Union's duty to protect states (p.273).
C and D are interchanged: 357 concerns legislative powers under Article 356 and 359A the repealed Punjab provision (p.273).
A and C are exchanged: 354 is revenue distribution, 357 is legislative powers under Article 356 (p.273).
